comments.body:
Hi @rdehuyss,

### Root Cause
The failure during `docker compose up` (specifically when building the `web-ui` image) was caused by `Dockerfile.web-ui` executing:
```dockerfile
RUN npm ci
```
The `npm ci` command strictly requires an existing `package-lock.json` file. However, `whatsapp-web-ui/` only contained `package.json`, causing npm to fail with `npm error code EUSAGE`.

### Fix
1. Generated and committed `whatsapp-web-ui/package-lock.json` to the repository.
2. Updated `Dockerfile.web-ui` to gracefully fall back:
```dockerfile
RUN if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then npm ci; else npm install; fi
```

Both fixes are now merged to `main` in commit `3dc7867`. Pull the latest `main` and `docker compose up --build` will now build cleanly. Thank you for reporting this!

comments.body:
Looked into this against current code -- looks like it's already resolved, not still open work:

- `whatsapp-bridge/internal/whatsapp/client.go` uses whatsmeow's `sqlstore` container backed by `store/whatsapp.db`, calling `container.GetFirstDevice()` first and only falling back to `NewDevice()` (fresh pairing) if no device exists. Auth/identity/session keys persist to SQLite across restarts, not just in memory.
- `docker-compose.yaml` bind-mounts `./store:/app/whatsapp-bridge/store` on the bridge service, so the store survives container restarts/recreates, not just process restarts.
- `Dockerfile.bridge`'s entrypoint explicitly `chown`/`chmod`s the mounted `store/` dir before dropping to the non-root `appuser` -- handles the classic bind-mount-permission-mismatch failure mode that would otherwise silently break persistence for non-root containers.
- README already documents the distinction between what causes re-auth (phone offline >14 days, manual unlink, WhatsApp-side revocation, forced app update) and what doesn't (restart, idle disconnect, container restart), plus a troubleshooting section for "needs re-pairing after restart" that correctly attributes that case to server-side revocation, not local state loss.

Verified this isn't just a code-reading conclusion -- restarted a live bridge instance (both a plain process restart and a full binary/working-directory relocation) and confirmed `needs_pairing: false` and immediate reauthentication from the stored session both times, no QR/pairing-code needed.

Looks safe to close unless there's a specific reproduction case this was tracking that isn't covered by the above (e.g. a particular deployment target with a non-persistent filesystem) -- happy to dig into that if so.

comments.body: the conditional-JOIN-with-unconditional-SELECT pattern is the classic SQLite builder trap. every codebase building queries by string concat hits it because SELECT gets treated as scaffolding and JOINs get treated as features, when they're the same thing. option B is structurally right, not just simpler. the real issue is include_last_message doing two jobs: shape-of-return and shape-of-SQL. those should separate. skip the JOIN when you don't need rows AND stop projecting those columns; shape output in python after fetch. mixing the two is what produced this bug and will produce the next.
Thanks for the detailed repro and root-cause analysis. Confirmed locally. We shipped a fix for the include_last_message=False SQL path and added regression tests so this branch won’t regress again.
Fixed in #40. Thanks again for clear repro + analysis.

comments.body:
Updating this with a correction — the gitleaks half of the original PR **didn't actually work**, and the way it failed is worth flagging.

`gitleaks-action@v2` pins gitleaks **8.24.3**. The global `[[allowlists]]` + `regexTarget = "match"` form I used isn't honoured on that version, but is on 8.30+. So it suppressed the finding on a current local gitleaks and did nothing in CI. The green Security Scan here wasn't evidence either — PR runs scan only the pushed commits, so they never reach the commit that trips it. Only the scheduled run does a full-history scan.

I found this the hard way: I merged the same config into my fork, and the next Sunday cron failed anyway. The failing run's log shows the config being loaded and the leak still reported:

```
gitleaks version: 8.24.3
DBG using existing gitleaks config .gitleaks.toml from `(--source)/.gitleaks.toml`
WRN leaks found: 1
```

Now rewritten as a rule-scoped `[[rules]]` + `[rules.allowlist]` allowlist, which works on both versions, and narrowed to match the placeholder *values* rather than whole lines or file paths — so a real secret in a `.md` file still gets reported. Verified both ways on 8.24.3 and 8.30.1; the table in the description has the full matrix, including reproducing the old config's 2 findings at 8.24.3.

Also rebased onto current `main`.

Two things you should know: the `Lint` failure on this branch is pre-existing on `main` (ruff `I001` in `main.py` / `whatsapp.py`) and unrelated to this PR — happy to fix it here or separately. And FWIW `main` is failing this scan right now for the same reason, so this should go green on the next cron once merged.

Hi @simonseifert! 👋

First off, I want to sincerely apologize for the delay in getting back to you on this! I really appreciate the time and effort you put into rebasing PR #55 and PR #56, building the `mlx-whisper` integration, and developing the `sentence-transformers` semantic recall module.

After doing a deep architectural review of the project's long-term roadmap, we are establishing a clear design philosophy for `whatsapp-mcp-extended`: **Lean Transport Primitives**.

### 📐 The Core Philosophy
1. **Core `whatsapp-mcp-extended`:** Focused strictly on being a rock-solid, zero-bloat, cross-platform transport primitive for WhatsApp (socket lifecycle, messaging CRUD, raw media downloads, reactions, group administration, webhooks, and safety allowlists). It runs lightweight across Linux Docker containers, macOS, and Windows without platform-gated ML heavy dependencies.
2. **Plugins & Extensions:** High-level ML capabilities (voice-to-text, vector search, custom LLM processors) live in the new `plugins/` directory and as composable sidecars.

### 🌟 Highlighting Your Work
Your work is awesome and extremely useful for developers who want an all-in-one local setup! To make sure your work is featured prominently:
- We have added your recipes into the official [`plugins/`](https://github.com/FelixIsaac/whatsapp-mcp-extended/tree/main/plugins) directory.
- We have officially featured your fork [`simonseifert/whatsapp-mcp-pro`](https://github.com/simonseifert/whatsapp-mcp-pro) in `README.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md` as the recommended pre-packaged ML bundle for users who want an all-in-one setup!
- You are credited in **Community Acknowledgements**.

Thank you so much again for being such a core part of this open-source community! 🙏

Your PR was the **first working end-to-end media download implementation** in any fork of this project. The HKDF-SHA256 → HMAC verify → AES-256-CBC → PKCS#7 unpadding pipeline you wrote proved the approach was feasible, and the path traversal protection and timeout-bounded client showed real production thinking.

We ultimately landed a whatsmeow-native `Download()` call (which avoids re-implementing the crypto layer manually), but your implementation was the foundation that others built on. You're credited by name in the README's Community Acknowledgements section for exactly this reason.

Thanks for doing the hard work of verifying it end-to-end with real WhatsApp media. That kind of validation matters.
